page: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with a dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. The instance provides 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1D cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 480 MB of L3 cache. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX).

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities and high memory bandwidth. The instance achieved a strong multi-core CPU score of 69359.48 in stress-ng and 20583.0 in Geekbench. Memory read bandwidth is strong, reaching 5112.66 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 197.6 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, though large block write bandwidth is average at 79.1 GB/sec. The system demonstrates top-tier performance in static web serving throughput at 105.74 GB/sec and image processing. Single-core performance is average, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 2133.99. For LLM inference, prompt processing is highly efficient, reaching a top-tier 39.14 tokens/sec for large 70B models, while text generation for the same model is average at 3.52 tokens/sec.

The m8i-flex.16xlarge does not include local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and CPU-based computation. This hardware profile provides a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring high memory bandwidth and multi-threaded processing without the added cost of dedicated local disks or graphics hardware. Network connectivity is capped at a baseline of 15 Gbps. The instance is suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
